description: Welcome to Agri-Space Morocco! Based in Casablanca, we are building an innovative web platform for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. Our goal is to help Moroccan farmers combat drought and optimize irrigation using real-time NASA Earth observation datasets (NASA POWER, SMAP, and Landsat) through an accessible, sensor-free dashboard.
summary:
Agri-Space Morocco is a free, bilingual (English & Arabic) web application designed to help Moroccan farmers combat severe drought and adapt their agricultural practices using NASA Earth observation data—without requiring expensive hardware sensors. 

Built for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, the platform allows farmers to pinpoint their land on an interactive satellite map (powered by Esri World Imagery and Leaflet.js) and immediately access real-time climate data from the NASA POWER API alongside surface soil moisture (NASA SMAP) and vegetation health (Landsat/MODIS NDVI) analytics. Our smart recommendation engine translates these satellite metrics into plain-language irrigation schedules, water-saving tips, and drought-resilient crop suggestions suited for Moroccan regions.

By eliminating cost barriers and making space data accessible to smallholder farmers, Agri-Space Morocco preserves vital water resources and strengthens food security.
details:
### What It Does & How It Works

Agri-Space Morocco is a web-based agricultural intelligence and drought-monitoring platform designed to help Moroccan farmers make data-driven irrigation and crop-selection decisions without needing expensive hardware sensors. Users select any farm plot on an interactive satellite map of Morocco (or use quick-select buttons for major agricultural regions such as Souss-Massa, Gharb, Doukkala, Saïss, and Haouz). The application then fetches real-time climate data (solar radiation, temperature, and precipitation) from the NASA POWER API and pairs it with NASA SMAP surface soil moisture modeling and Landsat/MODIS NDVI vegetation health scores. Based on these indicators, a built-in recommendation engine generates practical irrigation schedules and suggests drought-resilient crops.

### Benefits & Intended Impact

Morocco faces severe multi-year droughts and acute water scarcity, while most smallholder farmers cannot afford IoT soil sensors. Agri-Space Morocco eliminates hardware barriers by providing free, satellite-backed field insights accessible from any smartphone or computer browser. The intended impact is to reduce water waste, prevent crop stress, and strengthen food security across rural communities in Morocco and similar arid regions.

### Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Languages & Frontend:HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript (ES6+).

- Mapping & Visualization: Leaflet.js with Esri World Imagery satellite tiles, and Chart.js for 7-day soil moisture and temperature trend charts.

- Data & Hosting:NASA POWER API, NASA SMAP & Landsat/MODIS datasets, and GitHub Pages for cloud deployment.

- **AI Assistance Disclosure:** Large Language Models (Claude AI and Gemini) were used to assist with code structuring, debugging, and text refinement, while Gamma was used to structure the presentation layout.

### Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Our creativity lies in translating complex Earth observation telemetry into simple, everyday farming actions—such as recommending specific local drought-resistant crops (olives, argan, carob, barley). Key factors considered during development included zero-cost accessibility, low-bandwidth performance as a lightweight single-page web app, and linguistic inclusivity through an instant English/Arabic toggle so local Moroccan farmers can actually use the tool in the field.
